t: You're looking at the Queen Eleanor Memorial Cross, in the forecourt of Charing Cross station. It was put up in 1864 and 1865 as a fanciful reconstruction of the medieval cross at Charing. That was one of twelve crosses Edward the First raised in memory of his first wife, Eleanor of Castile. Edward Middleton Barry designed it. He was also the architect of the station behind it. Thomas Earp carved the statues of Queen Eleanor. The original cross stood about 200 metres southwest of here. That spot is now taken by Hubert Le Sueur's statue of Charles the First, installed in 1675.
